source.text: וַיִּקְח֣וּ בְנֵֽי־אַ֠הֲרֹן נָדָ֨ב וַאֲבִיה֜וּא אִ֣ישׁ מַחְתָּת֗וֹ וַיִּתְּנ֤וּ בָהֵן֙ אֵ֔שׁ וַיָּשִׂ֥ימוּ עָלֶ֖יהָ קְטֹ֑רֶת וַיַּקְרִ֜בוּ לִפְנֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ אֵ֣שׁ זָרָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֧ר לֹ֦א צִוָּ֖ה אֹתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And took [the] sons of Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, each his censer, and put in them fire, and placed on it incense, and brought near before Yahweh strange fire which not he had commanded them.

en.L: And the sons of Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, took each his censer, and they put fire in them and placed incense on it, and they brought near before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} strange fire, which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had not commanded them.
en.B: Aaron's sons Nadab and Abihu each took his own censer. They put fire in it, laid incense on the fire, and offered before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} an improper fire, one {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had not commanded them to bring.
en.R: Nadab and Abihu, two of Aaron's sons, each took a pan for burning incense. They put fire in the pans and placed incense on top. Then they offered it before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. But it was the wrong kind of fire. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} had not commanded them to bring it.

es.L: Y los hijos de Aarón, Nadab y Abiú, tomaron cada uno su incensario, y pusieron en ellos fuego y colocaron sobre él incienso, y presentaron delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} fuego extraño, que no les había mandado.
es.B: Nadab y Abiú, hijos de Aarón, tomaron cada uno su propio incensario. Pusieron fuego en él, echaron incienso sobre el fuego y ofrecieron delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} un fuego no autorizado, un fuego que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} no les había mandado traer.
es.R: Nadab y Abiú, dos de los hijos de Aarón, tomaron cada uno un recipiente para quemar incienso. Pusieron fuego en los recipientes y colocaron incienso encima. Luego lo ofrecieron delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Pero no era el fuego correcto. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} no les había mandado traerlo.

fr.L: Et les fils d’Aaron, Nadab et Abihou, prirent chacun son encensoir, et ils y mirent du feu et posèrent de l’encens dessus, et ils firent approcher devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} un feu étranger, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne leur avait pas ordonné.
fr.B: Nadab et Abihou, fils d’Aaron, prirent chacun leur encensoir. Ils y mirent du feu, déposèrent de l’encens sur le feu et présentèrent devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} un feu non autorisé, un feu qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne leur avait pas ordonné d’apporter.
fr.R: Nadab et Abihou, deux des fils d’Aaron, ont pris chacun un récipient pour brûler l’encens. Ils y ont mis du feu et ont placé de l’encens dessus. Puis ils l’ont offert devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Mais ce n’était pas le bon feu. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ne leur avait pas ordonné de l’apporter.

sw.L: Na wana wa Haruni, Nadabu na Abihu, wakachukua kila mmoja chetezo chake, wakatia moto ndani yake, wakaweka uvumba juu yake, wakasogeza mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} moto wa kigeni, ambao hakuwa amewaamuru.
sw.B: Nadabu na Abihu, wana wa Haruni, walichukua kila mmoja chetezo chake. Wakatia moto ndani yake, wakaweka uvumba juu ya moto huo, wakatoa mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} moto usioruhusiwa, ambao hakuwa amewaamuru kuuleta.
sw.R: Nadabu na Abihu, wawili kati ya wana wa Haruni, walichukua kila mmoja chombo cha kufukizia uvumba. Wakatia moto ndani ya vyombo hivyo na kuweka uvumba juu yake. Kisha wakautoa mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Lakini haukuwa moto unaofaa. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} hakuwa amewaamuru kuuleta.

vi.L: Các con trai của A-rôn là Na-đáp và A-bi-hu, mỗi người lấy lư hương của mình, bỏ lửa vào, đặt hương lên trên, rồi dâng trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} một thứ lửa lạ mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không truyền cho họ.
vi.B: Na-đáp và A-bi-hu, các con trai của A-rôn, mỗi người lấy lư hương của mình, bỏ lửa vào, đặt hương lên lửa, rồi dâng trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} một thứ lửa không hợp lệ, là lửa {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không truyền cho họ dâng.
vi.R: Na-đáp và A-bi-hu là hai con trai của A-rôn. Mỗi người lấy một cái lư để đốt hương. Họ bỏ lửa vào lư rồi đặt hương lên trên. Sau đó họ dâng hương trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Nhưng đó là thứ lửa không đúng. {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã không truyền cho họ mang lửa ấy đến.

decisions.choice: strange fire: fire that was not permitted, outside what God had commanded
decisions.reason: The word describes what is outside, foreign or not allowed. It forbids "strange incense" on the incense altar (Exodus 30:9) and is used of someone who is not a priest coming near the sanctuary (Numbers 3:10, 38). The text does not say exactly what was wrong. It says only that God had not commanded it. The coals may not have come from the altar (compare 16:12), or the offering may have been made at a time or in a way God had not appointed.

decisions.choice: censer: a fire pan for carrying burning coals
decisions.reason: A censer was a shallow pan in which burning coals were carried and incense laid on them, so that its smoke rose before God (16:12-13; Numbers 16:6-7, 17-18).

decisions.choice: Nadab and Abihu: Aaron's two oldest sons
decisions.reason: They were Aaron's firstborn and second sons (Exodus 6:23). They had gone up the mountain with Moses and seen God (Exodus 24:1, 9-11), and they were ordained as priests with their father in chapter 8. Their death is remembered in 16:1; Numbers 3:4; 26:61.

decisions.choice: an improper fire (Balanced); the wrong kind of fire (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Strange" today suggests something odd. The point is that the fire was not permitted, so Balanced says "improper" and Readable "the wrong kind of". Literal keeps "strange fire".

decisions.choice: two of Aaron's sons; a pan for burning incense
decisions.reason: Aaron had four sons (Exodus 6:23), so Readable says "two of". It explains "censer" by what it was used for.

decisions.choice: "fuego extraño" (L); "un fuego no autorizado" (B); "no era el fuego correcto" (R)
decisions.reason: The word means foreign, outside what is allowed (m1). Literal keeps "extraño"; Balanced says plainly that the fire was not permitted, and Readable that it was the wrong fire, as the English levels do.

decisions.choice: passé simple for the narrative at Literal and Balanced ("prirent", "mirent", "firent approcher"); passé composé at Readable ("ont pris", "ont mis")
decisions.reason: As docs/french-style.md section 3, for the narrative of chapter 10. The speeches within it (Moses, God, Aaron) use the tenses of spoken French.

decisions.choice: "un feu étranger" (L); "un feu non autorisé" (B); "ce n'était pas le bon feu" (R)
decisions.reason: The word means foreign, outside what is allowed (m1). Literal keeps "étranger", which in French can still mean "not belonging here"; Balanced says plainly that the fire was not permitted, and Readable that it was the wrong fire, as the English levels do.

decisions.choice: "moto wa kigeni" (L); "moto usioruhusiwa" (B); "haukuwa moto unaofaa" (R)
decisions.reason: The word means foreign, outside what is allowed (m1). Literal keeps "wa kigeni" (foreign); Balanced says the fire was not permitted, and Readable that it was not the right fire, as the English levels do. "Chetezo" (censer) at Literal and Balanced; Readable explains it as "chombo cha kufukizia uvumba".

decisions.choice: "lư hương" (censer)
decisions.reason: The common Vietnamese word for a vessel that holds burning incense; Readable says what it is for, "một cái lư để đốt hương".

decisions.choice: "{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}" with "phán" for God speaking, "Ngài" for him in the narrative
decisions.reason: As in Genesis: the divine name in capitals with "Gia-vê" as the setting alternative; "phán" is kept for God speaking, "nói" for everyone else. Recorded once for Leviticus 10-15.

source.text: וַתֵּ֥צֵא אֵ֛שׁ מִלִּפְנֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה וַתֹּ֣אכַל אוֹתָ֑ם וַיָּמֻ֖תוּ לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And went out fire from before Yahweh and consumed them, and they died before Yahweh.

en.L: And fire went out from before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and consumed them, and they died before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Then fire went out from before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and devoured them, and they died in the presence of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Then fire came out from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and burned them up. They died there in front of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Y salió fuego de delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y los consumió, y murieron delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.B: Entonces salió fuego de delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y los devoró, y murieron en presencia {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.R: Entonces salió fuego {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y los quemó. Murieron allí, delante {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Et un feu sortit de devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} et les consuma, et ils moururent devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Alors un feu sortit de devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} et les dévora, et ils moururent en présence {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Alors un feu est sorti {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} et les a brûlés. Ils sont morts là, devant {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Na moto ukatoka mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ukawala, nao wakafa mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Ndipo moto ulitoka mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ukawala kabisa, nao wakafa mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Ndipo moto ulitoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ukawachoma. Wakafa pale pale mbele za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

vi.L: Lửa từ trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phát ra và thiêu nuốt họ, và họ chết trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.B: Bấy giờ lửa từ trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phát ra thiêu nuốt họ, và họ chết trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.R: Rồi lửa từ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phát ra thiêu cháy họ. Họ chết ngay tại đó, trước mặt {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.

decisions.choice: fire went out from before Yahweh and consumed: the same words as 9:24
decisions.reason: In 9:24 fire went out from before Yahweh and consumed the offerings on the altar, and the people shouted for joy. Now the same fire consumes the two priests who brought what God had not commanded. The fire that showed God's acceptance also shows his holiness (verse 3).

decisions.choice: consumed: killed them by fire
decisions.reason: The verb means to eat up or devour, and here to kill by fire. The bodies were not reduced to ashes: in verse 5 they are carried out still in their tunics.

decisions.choice: devoured
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for eating. "Devoured" keeps the picture; Literal has "consumed" and Readable "burned them up".

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶֽל־אַהֲרֹ֗ן הוּא֩ אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֨ר יְהוָ֤ה׀לֵאמֹר֙ בִּקְרֹבַ֣י אֶקָּדֵ֔שׁ וְעַל־פְּנֵ֥י כָל־הָעָ֖ם אֶכָּבֵ֑ד וַיִּדֹּ֖ם אַהֲרֹֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Moses to Aaron, it [is] what spoke Yahweh, saying, by those near me I will show myself holy, and before [the] face of all the people I will be glorified. And was silent Aaron.

en.L: And Moses said to Aaron, "This [is] what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke, saying, 'Among those near to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} I will show myself holy, and before all the people I will be glorified.'" And Aaron was silent.
en.B: Moses said to Aaron, "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} meant when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, 'Through those who come near {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} I will show that I am holy, and in the sight of all the people I will show {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} glory.'" And Aaron said nothing.
en.R: Moses said to Aaron, "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was talking about when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, 'I will show that I am holy to those who come near {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. I will show {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} glory to all the people.'" Aaron did not say a word.

es.L: Y dijo Moisés a Aarón: «Esto [es] lo que habló {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, diciendo: “En los que están cerca de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} mostraré santo, y delante de todo el pueblo seré glorificado”». Y Aarón calló.
es.B: Moisés le dijo a Aarón: «Esto es lo que quiso decir {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} cuando dijo: “Por medio de los que se acercan a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} mostraré que soy santo, y a la vista de todo el pueblo mostraré {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} gloria”». Y Aarón no dijo nada.
es.R: Moisés le dijo a Aarón: «De esto hablaba {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} cuando dijo: “Mostraré que soy santo a los que se acercan a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. Mostraré {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} gloria a todo el pueblo”». Aarón no dijo ni una palabra.

fr.L: Et Moïse dit à Aaron : « C’[est] ce dont {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a parlé, en disant : “Parmi ceux qui sont proches de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} montrerai saint, et devant tout le peuple je serai glorifié.” » Et Aaron se tut.
fr.B: Moïse dit à Aaron : « Voilà ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} voulait dire quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a déclaré : “À travers ceux qui s’approchent de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, je montrerai que je suis saint, et aux yeux de tout le peuple je manifesterai {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} gloire.” » Et Aaron ne dit rien.
fr.R: Moïse a dit à Aaron : « Voici de quoi {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} parlait quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a dit : “Je montrerai que je suis saint à ceux qui s’approchent de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. Je montrerai {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} gloire à tout le peuple.” » Aaron n’a pas dit un mot.

sw.L: Musa akamwambia Haruni, "Hili [ndilo] alilolinena {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, akisema, 'Kwa wale walio karibu {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitajionyesha kuwa mtakatifu, na mbele ya watu wote nitatukuzwa.'" Naye Haruni akanyamaza.
sw.B: Musa alimwambia Haruni, "Hiki ndicho {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alichomaanisha aliposema, 'Kupitia wale wanaonikaribia nitaonyesha kwamba {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ni mtakatifu, na machoni pa watu wote nitaonyesha utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}.'" Haruni hakusema chochote.
sw.R: Musa alimwambia Haruni, "Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alilokuwa akizungumzia aliposema, 'Nitaonyesha kwamba {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ni mtakatifu kwa wale wanaonikaribia. Nitaonyesha utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} kwa watu wote.'" Haruni hakusema neno lolote.

vi.L: Môi-se nói với A-rôn: "Đây [là] điều {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phán rằng: 'Giữa những người đến gần {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ tỏ mình là thánh, và trước mặt toàn dân {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ được tôn vinh.'" A-rôn im lặng.
vi.B: Môi-se nói với A-rôn: "Đây là điều {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} muốn nói khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} phán: 'Qua những người đến gần {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ tỏ ra {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là thánh, và trước mặt toàn dân {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ bày tỏ vinh quang của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.'" A-rôn không nói gì.
vi.R: Môi-se nói với A-rôn: "Đây là điều {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phán: 'Ta sẽ cho những người đến gần {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thấy {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là thánh. Ta sẽ bày tỏ vinh quang của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cho toàn dân thấy.'" A-rôn không nói một lời nào.

decisions.choice: among those near me I will show myself holy: God's holiness is shown in and through the priests
alternatives: among those near me I will be treated as holy
decisions.reason: "Those near" God are the priests who serve him (Exodus 19:22; Ezekiel 42:13). The verb means to show oneself holy or to be treated as holy. God is shown to be holy when those who come near him obey him, and, as here, when he judges those who do not treat him as holy (Numbers 20:12-13; Ezekiel 28:22).

decisions.choice: what Yahweh spoke: a saying not found word for word earlier
decisions.reason: No earlier passage has these exact words. The nearest are Exodus 19:22, where the priests who come near must keep themselves holy, and Exodus 29:43-44, where God says the tent will be made holy by his glory. Moses may be summing up such words, or quoting a saying not recorded elsewhere. The verb "I will be glorified" is the one used when God gains glory over Pharaoh (Exodus 14:4, 17-18).

decisions.choice: Aaron was silent: he did not protest or cry out
decisions.reason: Aaron makes no answer and no lament. His silence accepts what has happened, as the commands of verses 6-7 will require of him.

decisions.choice: show my glory
decisions.reason: The passive "I will be glorified" is put actively, God showing his glory, which is how he gains it (Exodus 14:4). Literal keeps the passive.

source.text: וַיִּקְרָ֣א מֹשֶׁ֗ה אֶל־מִֽישָׁאֵל֙ וְאֶ֣ל אֶלְצָפָ֔ן בְּנֵ֥י עֻזִּיאֵ֖ל דֹּ֣ד אַהֲרֹ֑ן וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֗ם קִ֠רְב֞וּ שְׂא֤וּ אֶת־אֲחֵיכֶם֙ מֵאֵ֣ת פְּנֵי־הַקֹּ֔דֶשׁ אֶל־מִח֖וּץ לַֽמַּחֲנֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And called Moses to Mishael and to Elzaphan, [the] sons of Uzziel, [the] uncle of Aaron, and said to them, come near, carry your brothers from before the holy place to outside the camp.

en.L: And Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan, the sons of Uzziel, the uncle of Aaron, and said to them, "Come near, carry your brothers from before the holy place to outside the camp."
en.B: Moses sent for Mishael and Elzaphan, the sons of Uzziel, who was Aaron's uncle. He told them, "Come forward and take your relatives from in front of the sanctuary, and carry them out of the camp."
en.R: Moses called for Mishael and Elzaphan. They were sons of Uzziel, Aaron's uncle. Moses said to them, "Come here. Carry the bodies of your relatives away from the front of the holy tent. Take them outside the camp."

es.L: Y llamó Moisés a Misael y a Elzafán, hijos de Uziel, tío de Aarón, y les dijo: «{{plural_you:Acérquense|Acercaos}}, {{plural_you:lleven|llevad}} a {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} hermanos de delante del lugar santo hasta fuera del campamento».
es.B: Moisés mandó llamar a Misael y a Elzafán, hijos de Uziel, el tío de Aarón. Les dijo: «{{plural_you:Vengan|Venid}} y {{plural_you:saquen|sacad}} a {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} parientes de delante del santuario; {{plural_you:llévenlos|llevadlos}} fuera del campamento».
es.R: Moisés llamó a Misael y a Elzafán. Eran hijos de Uziel, el tío de Aarón. Moisés les dijo: «{{plural_you:Vengan|Venid}} aquí. {{plural_you:Saquen|Sacad}} los cuerpos de {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} parientes de delante de la tienda santa. {{plural_you:Llévenlos|Llevadlos}} fuera del campamento».

fr.L: Et Moïse appela Mishaël et Eltsaphân, les fils d’Ouzziel, l’oncle d’Aaron, et il leur dit : « Approchez, emportez vos frères de devant le lieu saint jusqu’en dehors du camp. »
fr.B: Moïse fit venir Mishaël et Eltsaphân, fils d’Ouzziel, l’oncle d’Aaron. Il leur dit : « Avancez, enlevez vos parents de devant le sanctuaire et emportez-les hors du camp. »
fr.R: Moïse a appelé Mishaël et Eltsaphân. C’étaient des fils d’Ouzziel, l’oncle d’Aaron. Moïse leur a dit : « Venez ici. Enlevez de devant la tente sainte les corps de vos parents. Emmenez-les hors du camp. »

sw.L: Musa akawaita Mishaeli na Elsafani, wana wa Uzieli, baba mdogo wa Haruni, akawaambia, "Sogeeni, wabebeni ndugu zenu kutoka mbele ya mahali patakatifu mpaka nje ya kambi."
sw.B: Musa aliwaita Mishaeli na Elsafani, wana wa Uzieli, baba mdogo wa Haruni. Akawaambia, "Njooni mbele, mwaondoe jamaa zenu mbele ya mahali patakatifu, mkawapeleke nje ya kambi."
sw.R: Musa aliwaita Mishaeli na Elsafani. Walikuwa wana wa Uzieli, baba mdogo wa Haruni. Musa akawaambia, "Njooni hapa. Ondoeni maiti za jamaa zenu mbele ya hema takatifu. Wapelekeni nje ya kambi."

vi.L: Môi-se gọi Mi-sa-ên và Ên-xa-phan, các con trai của U-xi-ên, chú của A-rôn, và nói với họ: "Hãy đến gần, khiêng anh em của các anh từ trước Nơi Thánh ra ngoài trại quân."
vi.B: Môi-se cho gọi Mi-sa-ên và Ên-xa-phan, là các con trai của U-xi-ên, chú của A-rôn. Ông bảo họ: "Hãy đến đây, khiêng những người bà con của các anh khỏi phía trước Nơi Thánh và đem ra ngoài trại quân."
vi.R: Môi-se gọi Mi-sa-ên và Ên-xa-phan đến. Họ là con trai của U-xi-ên, chú của A-rôn. Môi-se nói với họ: "Hãy lại đây. Hãy khiêng xác hai người bà con của các anh ra khỏi chỗ phía trước lều thánh. Hãy đem họ ra ngoài khu trại."

decisions.choice: your brothers: your relatives
decisions.reason: Uzziel was a brother of Amram, Aaron's father (Exodus 6:18, 20, 22), so Mishael and Elzaphan were Aaron's cousins and close relatives of Nadab and Abihu. "Brothers" is used of kinsmen in this way (Genesis 13:8). They were Levites but not priests. Aaron and his remaining sons could not leave their service (verse 7), and a priest was not to make himself unclean by touching a dead body (21:1, 10-11).

decisions.choice: the holy place: the sanctuary, the tent and its court
decisions.reason: Here the word means the sanctuary in general. Nadab and Abihu died "before Yahweh" (verse 2), at the tent or in the court near the altar, and their bodies are carried from there out of the camp.

decisions.choice: the bodies of; the holy tent
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that the men carried the bodies, and calls the sanctuary "the holy tent".

decisions.choice: "baba mdogo wa Haruni" for "uncle"
decisions.reason: Uzziel was the brother of Amram, Aaron's father (m1), and the youngest of Kohath's sons (Exodus 6:18). Swahili names a father's younger brother "baba mdogo"; "mjomba" is properly a mother's brother.

decisions.choice: Moses addresses his kinsmen and Aaron's family as "các anh" (Aaron alone "anh"), and speaks of himself as "tôi"
decisions.reason: They are Moses' cousins and his brother's household, not the people at large; "các ngươi" is kept for God's commands. Used through Leviticus 10.

decisions.choice: "Nơi Thánh" (the holy place); Readable "lều thánh"
decisions.reason: The sanctuary term of the Pentateuch term sheet; Readable says plainly that it is the holy tent, as the English Readable does.

source.text: וַֽיִּקְרְב֗וּ וַיִּשָּׂאֻם֙ בְּכֻתֳּנֹתָ֔ם אֶל־מִח֖וּץ לַֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר דִּבֶּ֥ר מֹשֶֽׁה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they came near and carried them in their tunics to outside the camp, as had spoken Moses.

en.L: And they came near and carried them in their tunics to outside the camp, as Moses had spoken.
en.B: They came forward and carried them out of the camp in their own tunics, just as Moses had said.
en.R: So they came and carried the bodies outside the camp. The dead men were still dressed in their priests' tunics. The two men did just what Moses had said.

es.L: Y se acercaron y los llevaron en sus túnicas hasta fuera del campamento, como había dicho Moisés.
es.B: Se acercaron y los sacaron del campamento en sus propias túnicas, tal como Moisés había dicho.
es.R: Así que vinieron y llevaron los cuerpos fuera del campamento. Los muertos todavía tenían puestas sus túnicas de sacerdotes. Los dos hombres hicieron exactamente lo que Moisés había dicho.

fr.L: Et ils s’approchèrent et les emportèrent dans leurs tuniques jusqu’en dehors du camp, comme Moïse l’avait dit.
fr.B: Ils s’avancèrent et les emportèrent hors du camp, vêtus de leurs propres tuniques, comme Moïse l’avait dit.
fr.R: Ils sont donc venus et ont emporté les corps hors du camp. Les morts portaient encore leurs tuniques de prêtres. Les deux hommes ont fait exactement ce que Moïse avait dit.

sw.L: Wakasogea, wakawabeba katika kanzu zao mpaka nje ya kambi, kama Musa alivyosema.
sw.B: Walisogea mbele, wakawabeba nje ya kambi wakiwa wamevaa kanzu zao wenyewe, kama Musa alivyosema.
sw.R: Basi walikuja, wakazibeba maiti nje ya kambi. Wafu hao walikuwa bado wamevaa kanzu zao za ukuhani. Wale watu wawili walifanya sawasawa na Musa alivyosema.

vi.L: Họ đến gần và khiêng họ, trong áo dài của họ, ra ngoài trại quân, như Môi-se đã nói.
vi.B: Họ đến khiêng hai người ấy, vẫn mặc áo dài của mình, ra ngoài trại quân, đúng như lời Môi-se đã nói.
vi.R: Vậy họ đến và khiêng xác ra ngoài khu trại. Hai người chết vẫn còn mặc áo dài của thầy tế lễ. Hai người kia làm đúng như Môi-se đã nói.

decisions.choice: their tunics: the dead priests' own tunics
decisions.reason: "Their" most likely refers to Nadab and Abihu, who were wearing the priests' tunics put on them at their ordination (8:13). The fire had killed them without burning up their clothes. The words could also refer to the tunics of the men who carried them, but the text says nothing of those.

decisions.choice: The dead men were still dressed in their priests' tunics
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear whose tunics are meant, as in the meaning decision.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֣ה אֶֽל־אַהֲרֹ֡ן וּלְאֶלְעָזָר֩ וּלְאִֽיתָמָ֨ר׀בָּנָ֜יו רָֽאשֵׁיכֶ֥ם אַל־תִּפְרָ֣עוּ׀וּבִגְדֵיכֶ֤ם לֹֽא־תִפְרֹ֨מוּ֙ וְלֹ֣א תָמֻ֔תוּ וְעַ֥ל כָּל־הָעֵדָ֖ה יִקְצֹ֑ף וַאֲחֵיכֶם֙ כָּל־בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל יִבְכּוּ֙ אֶת־הַשְּׂרֵפָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר שָׂרַ֥ף יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Moses to Aaron and to Eleazar and to Ithamar his sons, your heads do not let loose, and your garments not you must tear, and not you will die, and on all the congregation he will be angry; and your brothers, all the house of Israel, will weep [for] the burning which burned Yahweh.

en.L: And Moses said to Aaron and to Eleazar and to Ithamar, his sons, "Do not let [the hair of] your heads hang loose, and do not tear your garments, so that you do not die and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is not angry with all the congregation. But your brothers, the whole house of Israel, may weep for the burning that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has burned.
en.B: Then Moses said to Aaron and his sons Eleazar and Ithamar, "Do not let your hair hang loose or tear your clothes in mourning, or you will die, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be angry with the whole congregation. Your relatives, the whole house of Israel, may weep over the burning {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has brought about.
en.R: Then Moses said to Aaron and his sons Eleazar and Ithamar, "Do not show your grief by letting your hair hang loose or by tearing your clothes. If you do, you will die, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will be angry with all the people. But your relatives, all the people of Israel, may cry over those {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} burned with fire.

es.L: Y dijo Moisés a Aarón, y a Eleazar y a Itamar, sus hijos: «No {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} sueltos [los cabellos de] {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} cabezas, y no {{plural_you:rasguen|rasguéis}} {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} vestidos, para que no {{plural_you:mueran|muráis}} y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} no se enoje contra toda la comunidad. Pero {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} hermanos, toda la casa de Israel, llorarán el incendio que ha encendido {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: Entonces Moisés dijo a Aarón y a sus hijos Eleazar e Itamar: «No {{plural_you:se suelten|os soltéis}} el cabello ni {{plural_you:rasguen|rasguéis}} {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} ropas en señal de duelo, o {{plural_you:morirán|moriréis}}, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se enojará con toda la comunidad. {{plural_you:Sus|Vuestros}} parientes, toda la casa de Israel, pueden llorar por el fuego que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha enviado.
es.R: Luego Moisés dijo a Aarón y a sus hijos Eleazar e Itamar: «No {{plural_you:muestren|mostréis}} {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} dolor con el cabello suelto ni con la ropa rasgada. Si lo {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}}, {{plural_you:morirán|moriréis}}, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} se enojará con todo el pueblo. Pero {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} parientes, todo el pueblo de Israel, pueden llorar por los que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} quemó con fuego.

fr.L: Et Moïse dit à Aaron, et à Éléazar et à Ithamar, ses fils : « Ne laissez pas flotter [les cheveux de] vos têtes, et ne déchirez pas vos vêtements, afin que vous ne mouriez pas et qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne s’irrite pas contre toute la communauté. Mais vos frères, toute la maison d’Israël, pleureront l’incendie qu’a allumé {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Puis Moïse dit à Aaron et à ses fils Éléazar et Ithamar : « Ne laissez pas vos cheveux dénoués et ne déchirez pas vos vêtements en signe de deuil, sinon vous mourrez, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’irritera contre toute la communauté. Vos parents, toute la maison d’Israël, pourront pleurer sur l’incendie que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a provoqué.
fr.R: Puis Moïse a dit à Aaron et à ses fils Éléazar et Ithamar : « Ne montrez pas votre chagrin en laissant vos cheveux défaits ou en déchirant vos vêtements. Sinon, vous mourrez, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} se mettra en colère contre tout le peuple. Mais vos parents, tout le peuple d’Israël, peuvent pleurer ceux que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a brûlés par le feu.

sw.L: Musa akamwambia Haruni, na Eleazari na Ithamari, wanawe, "Msiziache [nywele za] vichwa vyenu timtimu, wala msirarue mavazi yenu, msije mkafa, naye asije akaikasirikia jumuiya yote. Lakini ndugu zenu, nyumba yote ya Israeli, wataulilia moto ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameuwasha.
sw.B: Kisha Musa alimwambia Haruni na wanawe Eleazari na Ithamari, "Msiziache nywele zenu timtimu wala msirarue mavazi yenu kwa kuomboleza, la sivyo mtakufa, naye ataikasirikia jumuiya yote. Jamaa zenu, nyumba yote ya Israeli, wanaweza kuomboleza kwa ajili ya moto ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameuleta.
sw.R: Kisha Musa alimwambia Haruni na wanawe Eleazari na Ithamari, "Msionyeshe huzuni yenu kwa kuziacha nywele zenu timtimu au kwa kurarua mavazi yenu. Mkifanya hivyo, mtakufa, na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atawakasirikia watu wote. Lakini jamaa zenu, watu wote wa Israeli, wanaweza kuwalilia wale ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwachoma kwa moto.

vi.L: Môi-se nói với A-rôn, và với Ê-lê-a-sa và Y-tha-ma, các con trai của ông: "Đừng xõa [tóc trên] đầu các anh, và đừng xé áo các anh, để các anh khỏi chết và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không nổi giận với cả hội chúng. Nhưng anh em của các anh, là cả nhà Y-sơ-ra-ên, hãy khóc về sự thiêu đốt mà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã thiêu đốt.
vi.B: Môi-se nói với A-rôn và hai con trai ông là Ê-lê-a-sa và Y-tha-ma: "Đừng xõa tóc hay xé áo để tang, kẻo các anh phải chết và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nổi giận với cả hội chúng. Còn bà con của các anh, là cả nhà Y-sơ-ra-ên, được khóc thương về đám lửa mà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã giáng xuống.
vi.R: Rồi Môi-se nói với A-rôn và hai con trai ông là Ê-lê-a-sa và Y-tha-ma: "Đừng tỏ ra buồn rầu bằng cách xõa tóc hay xé áo. Nếu làm vậy, các anh sẽ chết, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ nổi giận với cả dân chúng. Nhưng bà con của các anh, là toàn dân Y-sơ-ra-ên, có thể khóc thương những người đã bị {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} thiêu chết.

decisions.choice: let the hair hang loose and tear the clothes: the usual signs of mourning
decisions.reason: Loosening the hair (or baring the head) and tearing one's clothes were signs of grief for the dead. The priest of highest rank was never to do them (21:10), and the person with a skin disease had to do them (13:45). Aaron and his sons are on duty in the sanctuary and may not mourn in this way.

decisions.choice: he will be angry with all the congregation: God, with the whole people
decisions.reason: The subject is God, though he is not named. If the priests broke his commands, his anger would fall on the whole people they serve, as a priest's sin brings guilt on the people (4:3).

decisions.choice: the burning that Yahweh has burned: the fire by which he struck them
decisions.reason: The people may mourn for Nadab and Abihu, though the priests on duty may not. "The burning" is the fire by which God killed them.

decisions.choice: in mourning (Balanced); show your grief by (Readable)
decisions.reason: The actions are signs of mourning, so Balanced and Readable say so. Readable names the LORD where the Hebrew has only "he", and says "all the people" for the congregation.

decisions.choice: "pleureront l'incendie qu'a allumé le SEIGNEUR" (L); "pleurer sur l'incendie que le SEIGNEUR a provoqué" (B)
alternatives: la brûlure que le SEIGNEUR a brûlée
decisions.reason: French cannot repeat the Hebrew "the burning that he burned" (m3) naturally; "incendie" with "allumer" or "provoquer" keeps the fire as God's doing. Readable says who was burned, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "kuziacha nywele timtimu" for letting the hair hang loose
decisions.reason: "Timtimu" is the Swahili word for hair left loose and dishevelled, the sign of grief described in m1.

source.text: וּמִפֶּתַח֩ אֹ֨הֶל מוֹעֵ֜ד לֹ֤א תֵֽצְאוּ֙ פֶּן־תָּמֻ֔תוּ כִּי־שֶׁ֛מֶן מִשְׁחַ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה עֲלֵיכֶ֑ם וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֖וּ כִּדְבַ֥ר מֹשֶֽׁה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And from [the] entrance of [the] tent of meeting not you must go out, lest you die, for [the] oil of anointing of Yahweh [is] on you. And they did according to [the] word of Moses.

en.L: And from the entrance of the tent of meeting you must not go out, lest you die, for the anointing oil of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} [is] on you." And they did according to the word of Moses.
en.B: Do not leave your place at the entrance of the tent of meeting, or you will die, because you bear {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s anointing oil." They did as Moses said.
en.R: Do not leave the entrance of the meeting tent, or you will die. You have been anointed with {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s oil." So they did what Moses said.

es.L: Y de la entrada de la Tienda del Encuentro no {{plural_you:saldrán|saldréis}}, no sea que {{plural_you:mueran|muráis}}, porque el aceite de la unción {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} [está] sobre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}». E hicieron conforme a la palabra de Moisés.
es.B: No {{plural_you:dejen|dejéis}} {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} puesto a la entrada de la Tienda del Encuentro, o {{plural_you:morirán|moriréis}}, porque {{plural_you:llevan|lleváis}} el aceite de la unción {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}». Ellos hicieron como Moisés dijo.
es.R: No {{plural_you:se alejen|os alejéis}} de la entrada de la Tienda del Encuentro, o {{plural_you:morirán|moriréis}}. {{plural_you:Han|Habéis}} sido ungidos con el aceite {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}». Así que hicieron lo que Moisés dijo.

fr.L: Et de l’entrée de la tente de la Rencontre vous ne sortirez pas, de peur que vous ne mouriez, car l’huile d’onction {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} [est] sur vous. » Et ils firent selon la parole de Moïse.
fr.B: Ne quittez pas votre poste à l’entrée de la tente de la Rencontre, sinon vous mourrez, car vous portez l’huile d’onction {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. » Ils firent comme Moïse l’avait dit.
fr.R: Ne quittez pas l’entrée de la tente de la Rencontre, sinon vous mourrez. Vous avez été oints avec l’huile {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. » Et ils ont fait ce que Moïse avait dit.

sw.L: Wala msitoke mlangoni pa Hema la Kukutania, msije mkafa, kwa maana mafuta ya kupaka ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} [yako] juu yenu." Wakafanya sawasawa na neno la Musa.
sw.B: Msiondoke mahali penu kwenye mlango wa Hema la Kukutania, la sivyo mtakufa, kwa sababu mnayo mafuta ya kupaka ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} juu yenu." Wakafanya kama Musa alivyosema.
sw.R: Msiondoke kwenye mlango wa Hema la Kukutania, la sivyo mtakufa. Mmepakwa mafuta ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}." Basi wakafanya kama Musa alivyosema.

vi.L: Và từ lối vào Lều Hội Kiến các anh không được đi ra, kẻo các anh chết, vì dầu xức của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} [ở] trên các anh." Họ làm theo lời Môi-se.
vi.B: Các anh không được rời chỗ mình ở lối vào Lều Hội Kiến, kẻo phải chết, vì các anh đang mang dầu xức của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}." Họ làm đúng như lời Môi-se.
vi.R: Đừng rời khỏi lối vào Lều Hội Kiến, nếu không các anh sẽ chết. Các anh đã được xức dầu của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}." Vậy họ làm theo lời Môi-se.

decisions.choice: the anointing oil of Yahweh is on you: you are set apart for his service
decisions.reason: Aaron and his sons were anointed at their ordination (8:12, 30). Being anointed, they belong to God's service, and it comes before the duties of mourning a family member. The priest of highest rank is likewise never to leave the sanctuary for the dead (21:10-12).

decisions.choice: go out: leave the sanctuary, to bury or mourn
decisions.reason: The command is not to leave the sanctuary to join the burial or the mourning. The tent's entrance is where they serve (8:33-35).

decisions.choice: your place at; you bear
decisions.reason: Balanced words the command as staying at one's post and the oil as something the priests carry on them.

decisions.choice: "Lều Hội Kiến" at every level
decisions.reason: The term sheet's name for the tent of meeting, kept also at Readable (where the English says "meeting tent") so the same tent has one name.

decisions.choice: wine and strong drink: wine and other fermented drink, such as beer
decisions.reason: The second word means an intoxicating drink other than wine, most likely beer made from grain. The pair often go together (Numbers 6:3; Proverbs 20:1). Isaiah 28:7 describes priests who stagger from them.

decisions.choice: a statute forever: a lasting rule, explained in verses 10-11
decisions.reason: For the phrase see 3:17. The text does not say that Nadab and Abihu had been drinking. The rule stands as a lasting safeguard, and verses 10-11 give its purpose: priests must judge clearly between holy and common, clean and unclean. Ezekiel 44:21 repeats it.

decisions.choice: a rule for all time to come
decisions.reason: Readable combines "a statute forever" and "for your generations" in one phrase.

decisions.choice: "bebida fuerte" (L); "cerveza" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word is an intoxicating drink other than wine, most likely beer made from grain (m1). Literal keeps "bebida fuerte"; Balanced and Readable say "cerveza", as the English says "beer". "Licor" would suggest distilled spirits.

decisions.choice: "boisson forte" (L); "bière" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word is an intoxicating drink other than wine, most likely beer made from grain (m1). Literal keeps the traditional "boisson forte"; Balanced and Readable say "bière", as the English says "beer".

decisions.choice: "kileo" (L); "pombe" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word is an intoxicating drink other than wine, most likely beer made from grain (m1). Literal says "kileo" (an intoxicant); Balanced and Readable say "pombe", the ordinary word for beer brewed from grain.

decisions.choice: God's commands use "ngươi" / "các ngươi" with "phải" and "không được" ("chớ" only where the Literal is terse; "đừng" at Readable)
decisions.reason: As the Pentateuch term sheet sets for the laws; recorded once for Leviticus 10-15.

decisions.choice: "bia" (beer) at Readable; "rượu mạnh" at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is fermented drink other than wine, most often beer; Literal and Balanced keep the traditional "rượu mạnh".

decisions.choice: the holy and the common: what belongs to God and what is for ordinary use
decisions.reason: "Common" means ordinary, not set apart for God. It does not mean wicked. Holy and common is one pair; unclean and clean is another. Something common may be clean or unclean, but only what is clean may come near what is holy. See the note at 11:4 for clean and unclean.

decisions.choice: to separate: the priests' task of judging
decisions.reason: God himself "separated" light from darkness (Genesis 1:4). Now the priests must make such separations for Israel, and chapter 11 begins at once with clean and unclean animals (11:47). Ezekiel 22:26 condemns priests who failed to do this, and Ezekiel 44:23 restores the task.

decisions.choice: tell apart (Balanced); tell the difference (Readable)
decisions.reason: The verb means to separate; here, to distinguish and decide. Literal keeps "separate".

decisions.choice: "ce qui est profane" for the common
decisions.reason: In French "profane" is the exact word for what is not consecrated, the opposite of "sacré"; it does not mean impious (m1). "Commun" would be read as "shared" or "vulgar". Readable says "ce qui ne l'est pas", as the English Readable says "what is not holy".

decisions.choice: "cha kawaida" for the common
decisions.reason: "Cha kawaida" (ordinary) keeps the point of m1: what is not set apart for God, not something wicked or dirty. "Najisi" and "safi" are kept for the second pair.

decisions.choice: "ô uế" (unclean) and "tinh sạch" (clean)
decisions.reason: The ritual terms of the Pentateuch term sheet, used at every level through chapters 11-15 so the reader sees the same pair; "tẩy sạch" for the verb "purify".

decisions.reason: Teaching Israel was part of the priest's work (Deuteronomy 33:10; Malachi 2:7). The laws of chapters 11-15 are the kind of rulings priests had to teach.

decisions.reason: The phrase means through Moses as God's messenger.

records.literal_gloss: And spoke Moses to Aaron and to Eleazar and to Ithamar, his sons who were left, take the grain offering which remains from [the] fire offerings of Yahweh and eat it unleavened beside the altar, for most holy of holy things [is] it.

en.L: And Moses spoke to Aaron and to Eleazar and to Ithamar, his remaining sons, "Take the grain offering that is left over from the offerings by fire of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and eat it unleavened beside the altar, for it [is] a most holy [thing].
en.B: Moses said to Aaron and to his sons who were left, Eleazar and Ithamar, "Take the grain offering that remains from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s food offerings and eat it, made without yeast, beside the altar, because it is most holy.
en.R: Moses spoke to Aaron and his two sons who were still alive, Eleazar and Ithamar. He said, "Take the grain offering that is left from the food offerings burned on the fire for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Eat it beside the altar, made without yeast. It is very holy.

es.L: Y habló Moisés a Aarón, y a Eleazar y a Itamar, sus hijos que quedaban: «{{plural_you:Tomen|Tomad}} la ofrenda de cereal que queda de las ofrendas quemadas {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y {{plural_you:cómanla|comedla}} sin levadura junto al altar, porque [es] cosa santísima.
es.B: Moisés dijo a Aarón y a los hijos que le quedaban, Eleazar e Itamar: «{{plural_you:Tomen|Tomad}} la ofrenda de cereal que queda de las ofrendas quemadas {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} y {{plural_you:cómanla|comedla}} junto al altar, preparada sin levadura, porque es santísima.
es.R: Moisés habló con Aarón y con sus dos hijos que aún vivían, Eleazar e Itamar. Les dijo: «{{plural_you:Tomen|Tomad}} la ofrenda de cereal que sobra de las ofrendas quemadas en el fuego para {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}. {{plural_you:Cómanla|Comedla}} junto al altar, hecha sin levadura. Es muy santa.

fr.L: Et Moïse parla à Aaron, et à Éléazar et à Ithamar, ses fils qui restaient : « Prenez l’offrande végétale qui reste des offrandes consumées par le feu {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, et mangez-la sans levain à côté de l’autel, car c’[est] une [chose] très sainte.
fr.B: Moïse dit à Aaron et aux fils qui lui restaient, Éléazar et Ithamar : « Prenez l’offrande végétale qui reste après les offrandes consumées par le feu pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Mangez-la à côté de l’autel, en pains sans levain, car elle est très sainte.
fr.R: Moïse a parlé à Aaron et à ses deux fils encore en vie, Éléazar et Ithamar. Il leur a dit : « Prenez l’offrande végétale qui reste des offrandes brûlées sur le feu pour {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Mangez-la à côté de l’autel, faite sans levain. Elle est très sainte.

sw.L: Musa akasema na Haruni, na Eleazari na Ithamari, wanawe waliobaki, "Chukueni sadaka ya nafaka iliyobaki katika sadaka za {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} za kuteketezwa kwa moto, mkaile isiyotiwa chachu kando ya madhabahu, kwa maana [ni] takatifu kabisa.

decisions.choice: the grain offering that remains: the people's grain offering of 9:17
decisions.reason: A handful of it had been burned on the altar (9:17). The rest belonged to the priests as a most holy portion, to be eaten without yeast in a holy place (2:3; 6:9). For the food offerings see 1:9, and for "most holy" see 2:3.

decisions.choice: remaining ... remains: the same word for the sons and the offering
decisions.reason: The two sons "who were left" alive and the grain offering "that remains" are described with the same verb. After the deaths of verse 2, Moses sees that the surviving priests still carry out the day's duties.

decisions.choice: "que quedaban" / "que queda"
decisions.reason: The sons "who were left" and the offering "that remains" share one Hebrew verb (m2). Spanish keeps the echo with "quedar" in both places at Literal and Balanced; Readable says "que aún vivían", as the English does.

decisions.choice: "qui restaient" / "qui reste" (L); "qui lui restaient" / "qui reste" (B)
decisions.reason: The sons "who were left" and the offering "that remains" share one Hebrew verb (m2). French keeps the echo with "rester" in both places at Literal and Balanced; Readable says "encore en vie", as the English does.

decisions.choice: "waliobaki" / "iliyobaki"
decisions.reason: The sons "who were left" and the offering "that remains" share one Hebrew verb (m2). Swahili keeps the echo with "-baki" in both places at Literal and Balanced; Readable says "waliokuwa bado hai", as the English does.

decisions.choice: "tế lễ ngũ cốc" (grain offering), "của lễ dâng bằng lửa" (food offering)
decisions.reason: The offering names of the Pentateuch term sheet, kept the same at every level; Readable does not add "đốt trên lửa" again because "dâng bằng lửa" already says it.
